first.rationale: Current situation shows concurrent declines in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). While competitive pricing pressure exists, the primary objective is sustainable qualified revenue, not short-term SMB acquisition. Memory_91 demonstrated that activation_messaging directly improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action—this directly addresses the activation decline. Memory_86 showed onboarding shortening improved completion rates. Activation_messaging is lower-risk than promotional_pricing (which memory_73 flagged as pooling two cohorts, limiting confidence) and better targeted to the immediate problem than enterprise_sales_assist or referral_incentives. We verify memory_86 (onboarding completion mechanism) and memory_73 (to assess the actual quality/reliability of the promotional_pricing finding given the pooling caveat noted). This preserves the option to pivot to pricing if activation_messaging underperforms, while testing the lever most directly connected to reported metrics and past success. Standard_experiment scope is appropriate given the week-capacity constraint and the need for directional evidence.
